sources.title: MiniMax M2.5: Built for Real-World Productivity
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The February 12 launch identifies two M2.5 versions: standard at 50 TPS and Lightning at 100 TPS, with identical capability and different serving speed/cost. Combined with the exact highspeed product description and staff clarification, this maps the fast API version to the same underlying model, not a separate trained release.

sources.title: MiniMax M2.5 product page
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The M2.5 body explicitly identifies exactly two API versions, M2.5 and M2.5-highspeed, with identical results and different speed; its 50/100 TPS description matches the launch’s standard/Lightning pair. The same page links the shared M2.5 weights. Current M3 navigation does not change this legacy product evidence or prove endpoint operation.

sources.title: Will M2.5-Lightning be released?
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. MiniMax org member ryanlee-dev explicitly says Lightning trades more inference resources for speed while model parameters remain exactly the same. Together with the official exact-highspeed product page, this establishes a serving-tier relationship to M2.5.

sources.title: MiniMax M2.5 model-size discussion
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The official-org reply says all M2-series models have 230B parameters. Retain that nominal total; the discussion title’s 10B active figure is a community claim and is not the active-count basis.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 configuration
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the same-day fetched official current and pinned M2.5 configurations on October 27. Both are identical; all size-bearing layer, hidden, expert, head and vocabulary dimensions and top-8-of-256 routing match the official M2 base configuration. No weight shards were downloaded.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 reference implementation
sources.evidence: Implements decoder-only attention plus routed MoE; e_score_correction_bias is registered as a buffer. Token embedding and output weights are untied. No MTP module is constructed by this reference implementation.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 checkpoint index and shard headers
sources.evidence: All 96103 indexed keys were matched to bounded shard headers cached by audit303 and independently recounted here. There are 228689748992 reference-registered weight elements, 15872 routing-bias values and 13880064 FP8 scale entries. Buffer registration does not establish whether the routing values were originally learned. No MTP keys occur.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 Model License
sources.evidence: Named MiniMax Model License grants use, modification and redistribution subject to attribution, agreement and prohibited-use requirements. Header gives weights-version release date 2026-02-13; the card labels the license modified-mit.

sources.title: MiniMax OpenAI SDK compatibility
sources.evidence: Exact MiniMax-M2.5-highspeed ID remains in the multi-turn tool-call reasoning note, which requires preserving think content. Current supported-model/context table contains only M3 variants; it does not establish the former highspeed API limit.

sources.title: MiniMax Anthropic SDK compatibility
sources.evidence: States M2.5-series inputs are text and tool-call content, without image/video input, and M2.x thinking cannot be disabled. Current endpoint support table lists M3 variants only.

sources.title: MiniMax model release notes
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The February entry names the M2.5/M2.5-highspeed pair; later entries identify M2.7 and M3 successors, without an exact highspeed parameter comparison or a separate trained highspeed checkpoint.

sources.title: The MiniMax-M2 Series: Mini Activations Unleashing Max Real-World Intelligence
sources.evidence: Reopened revised report October 27, 2026. Sections 1, 2 and 9 specify M2’s 9.8B-active backbone and identify the evolution through M2.5/M2.7 as post-training/data/RL progression. Combined with matching base/M2.5 dimensions, this supports a labeled nominal 9.8B inference for M2.5. The highspeed serving relationship preserves it. Comparison tables report benchmark scores, not an alternative highspeed count.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2.5 model card and weights
sources.evidence: Official downloadable text-generation checkpoint, modified-mit card metadata, local serving instructions and tool-calling guide. Its automatic parameter counter is not a learned-weight count.

sources.title: Frozen Models.dev source lead
sources.evidence: Frozen catalog supplied 204800 API context and February 13 date. This lead is not independent primary verification.

sources.title: MiniMax retired model list
sources.evidence: FAQ table labels M2.5/highspeed retired. The notice separately says new-user access ends October 19 and final pay-as-you-go retirement is November 18, 2026; M Plan/Token Plan requests have been rerouted since October 19. These conflicting lifecycle presentations do not prove current endpoint operation.

sources.title: Vercel AI Gateway MiniMax M2.5 highspeed provider metadata
sources.evidence: Exact primaryModel minimax-m2.5-highspeed with provider minimax has contextSize 204800 in embedded page data; rendered provider row rounds it to 205K. This establishes the advertised Vercel-to-MiniMax route limit, not independent native endpoint operation.

sources.title: MiniMax-M2 official base configuration
sources.evidence: Independently compared the same-day fetched official JSON against current/pinned M2.5 configurations on October 27. All parameter-bearing dimensions and routing match: 62 layers, 3072 hidden, 1536 expert FFN, 256 experts/top8, 48 query and 8 KV heads, head dimension128 and vocabulary200064. Configuration identity corroborates the report’s explicit post-training lineage; it is not a new tensor census.

sources.title: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash later card and comparison table
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved with curl on October 27 after web-reader failure. Independently read specifications and the complete HTML comparison table. Its 428B/23B counts describe M3.1-Flash; the table has benchmark scores and no M2.5/highspeed activated-parameter column. No later-model size is transferred.

name.note: Exact API identifier. The launch called the fast serving version M2.5-Lightning; the matching two-version descriptions establish the alias relationship.

family.note: Retains the catalog family key; specifically part of MiniMax M2-series/M2.5.

release_date.note: Earliest public launch of the fast version alongside M2.5. February 13 in the weights license is a later checkpoint-version date, not the earliest API announcement.

open_weights.note: Highspeed is a serving mode of the released M2.5 model. The official product page links the shared weights and the org reply rules out a separate Lightning parameter set.

license.note: Actual distributed license title. Model-card metadata still labels it modified-mit, but the distributed agreement contains its own notice and prohibited-use terms; this is not plain MIT. Hosted API terms are separate.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit retains developer nominal 230B total. Highspeed/Lightning is the same M2.5 model served with more inference resources, not a distinct trained parameter set. Neither the earlier storage subtotal nor the base report’s 229.9B is substituted as an exact total.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal lineage inference: the developer report identifies a 9.8B-active M2 backbone and post-training evolution through M2.5; matching official configurations corroborate preserved size and routing. The exact highspeed product description plus the official Lightning clarification establish unchanged model parameters. Follow the report’s main-model activation convention rather than a new embedding-dependent tensor sum. Later comparison tables add no conflicting target count.

architecture.note: Decoder-only Transformer with full grouped-query attention and routed MoE; 62 layers, 256 experts, eight selected per token. Lightning is a serving name and does not establish Lightning Attention.

context_window.note: Exact Vercel gateway metadata advertises 204800 for the MiniMax-backed highspeed route. Shared checkpoint native max_position_embeddings is 196608. Current native API tables removed this model, so this is a provider-specific hosted limit, not a fresh native-endpoint verification.

modalities.note: Text language model; MiniMax explicitly excludes image/video input for M2.5-series. Tool-call serialization does not add a sensory modality.

reasoning.note: Exact highspeed API note preserves think output; M2.x thinking is always enabled.

tool_call.note: Exact highspeed API note documents tool-call conversation handling, reinforced by release notes and shared-weight tool guide.

description.value: Faster serving version of MiniMax M2.5 for text reasoning, coding and tool-using agents, using the same underlying model parameters.
description.note: Replaces generic latency wording with the verified serving-mode relationship and supported capabilities.

patch.description: Faster serving version of MiniMax M2.5 for text reasoning, coding and tool-using agents, using the same underlying model parameters.
patch.notes: Highspeed/Lightning is a faster serving tier of M2.5 with unchanged model parameters. Total 230B is developer nominal; active 9.8B is inferred from the documented M2 post-training lineage and matching backbone dimensions/routing. Vercel gateway metadata advertises a 204800-token MiniMax-backed highspeed route; shared checkpoint max_position_embeddings is 196608. Native API tables removed the model. The FAQ labels it retired but also gives November 18 final pay-as-you-go retirement and October 19 access restrictions/plan rerouting. Shared downloadable weights use the MiniMax Model License; card metadata labels it modified-mit.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains nominal 230B total and recovers nominal 9.8B active through documented M2 post-training lineage, matching configurations and the unchanged-parameter highspeed/Lightning relationship. Proposes excluding highspeed as a serving-tier duplicate of MiniMax-M2.5, consistent with the catalog’s independent-model scope. All unrelated field assessments are preserved; earlier context, license and lifecycle qualifications remain.

catalog_exclusion.reason: MiniMax identifies highspeed as the faster API version of M2.5 with identical results. Its launch names the corresponding fast version Lightning, and the official organization clarification says it uses more inference resources with exactly unchanged model parameters. No separate trained highspeed checkpoint is documented. Exclude this serving-tier duplicate from independent release counts while preserving its frozen report and parameter findings.
